items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: Don Menza had told me that he did the same thing.

ctx.x: At this stage in your playing and your career, what do you find is interesting and useful to practice?

I practice things that are hard. I practice tunes that have different chord changes, things that don’t lay correctly. And they don’t lay naturally under my hands. And so I’ll work them slowly. Back when I was learning “Giant Steps” I practiced it as a ballad. And gradually got where the most comfortable transitions were. And that seems to work for a lot of people. Don Menza had told me that he did the same thing. So I think we all do things in a similar way, just like that Oriental martial arts thing where people…
Yeah, that’s interesting because I think it’s also probably very useful for playing the rests. Because rests are harder to play at slow tempos. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-
